record.original_question: Is the Atiyah-Jones conjecture true for every irrational complex surface, i.e. does the inclusion of the instanton moduli space of charge k into the corresponding gauge-theoretic configuration space induce isomorphisms in low-degree homology and homotopy in that setting?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective surface that is irrational (i.e., not birational to $\mathbb{P}^2$). For a compact Lie group $G$ (e.g. $G=SU(2)$), let $M_k(X)$ denote the moduli space of $G$-instantons of charge $k$ on $X$ (anti-self-dual connections on a principal $G$-bundle of second Chern class $k$, modulo gauge), and let $B_k(X)$ denote the corresponding gauge-theoretic configuration space of all connections modulo gauge (equivalently, the classifying space of based gauge transformations of the bundle). There is a natural inclusion $\theta_k : M_k(X) \hookrightarrow B_k(X)$.

The generalized Atiyah–Jones conjecture asserts that, for each fixed integer $q \ge 0$, there exists $k_0(q)$ such that for all $k \ge k_0(q)$ the map $\theta_k$ induces isomorphisms
$$H_q(M_k(X);\mathbb{Z}) \xrightarrow{\cong} H_q(B_k(X);\mathbb{Z}), \qquad \pi_q(M_k(X)) \xrightarrow{\cong} \pi_q(B_k(X)).$$

Question: Does this conjecture hold for every irrational complex surface $X$?
artifact.status_search_result: The Atiyah–Jones conjecture has been established for $S^4$ (Boyer–Hurtubise–Mann–Milgram), for ruled surfaces (Hurtubise–Milgram), for rational surfaces (Gasparim and collaborators), and for blown-up surfaces over base cases. No proof is known for irrational complex surfaces in general, and the question is listed as open.

status_evidence.title: Atiyah–Jones conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: proved for ruled surfaces by Hurtubise-Milgram and for rational surfaces by Gasparim; remains unproved for other types of 4-manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is known for rational and ruled surfaces but remains open for other 4-manifolds, including general irrational complex surfaces.

status_evidence.title: Atiyah Jones conjecture for blown-up surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Atiyah Jones conjecture for blown-up surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Progress is restricted to specific surface classes (rational, ruled, blown-up); the irrational case is not covered.
